To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

COPD is a common disease with a major impact on health care costs and patient quality of life; exacerbations are a key risk factor for early mortality and morbidity; there are many risk factors for exacerbations; and there are parallels in terms of risk factors and outcome trials between cardiovascular disease and COPD.
the prevalence and mortality of COPD is similar to that of cardiovascular disease (CVD), and the risk factors and management strategies for these diseases are comparable.

the risk factors for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are similar to those for cardiovascular disease, that there is a need to develop a multimodal approach for the management of exacerbations in COPD, and that large prospective trials based on hard outcomes are needed in COPD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epidemiology and pathogenesis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
the development of a comprehensive, evidence-based approach to COPD management, and the identification of high-risk patients for whom more intensive management strategies may be appropriate.
the development and evaluation of new treatments, particularly in the area of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current evidence base for the management of COPD is inadequate and that there is an urgent need for large-scale prospective trials that will help to improve clinical outcomes and quality of life for patients with this condition.
the management of patients with COPD is not as well defined as that for patients with cardiovascular disease.
COPD is an important and common disease with a significant impact on the health care system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the risk factors for COPD are similar to the risk factors for cardiovascular disease.
COPD is a chronic disease with a high mortality and morbidity, which has a high impact on the quality of life and the health care systems.
the management of COPD is evolving and improving, with the development of guidelines and evidence-based management strategies that are now being implemented in clinical practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of guidelines for the management of COPD is an evolving process and that, in particular, the role of the primary care physician is central.
the development of guidelines and management strategies for COPD has been hampered by the absence of large outcome studies and the lack of consensus about the most appropriate end points to use.
the management of COPD has much in common with the management of heart failure.
